title: eval-harness: CI prompt-regression enhancements and quality gating
author: Asha Patel
description:
Motivation: improve CI-side prompt-set regression detection and provide a lightweight quality gating mechanism that prevents merged changes from degrading eval metrics. This PR adds new CI hooks to run targeted prompt-set evaluations on changed prompt sets, surfaces metric deltas in the CI summary, and introduces an opt-in quality gate that can block merges when regressions exceed configured thresholds.

Summary of changes: - CI hooks: new GH Action workflows (eval/prompt-regression.yml) for incremental evaluation and metric diffing. - Eval runner: enhancements to the eval-harness to allow subset runs, stable seeding, and deterministic baseline selection. - Metrics: added normalized-metric computation and per-prompt breakdown for guardrails. - Quality gate: config file (.eval-gate.yaml) with thresholds and signal mapping. - Dashboard: small additions to CI artifact formatting to make metric diffs importable by the quality dashboard.

Checklist: - [x] Add incremental eval GH Action + matrix for changed prompt-sets - [x] Implement deterministic subset runner with seed control - [x] Emit CI-friendly metric-diffs and artifacts - [x] Add .eval-gate.yaml parsing and enforcement - [x] Unit tests and integration test workflow - [x] Docs skeleton in docs/eval-harness/ci-gates.md

Testing and validation: Ran full eval-harness suite on CI with synthetic prompt deltas to validate gate behavior. Confirmed metric stability across 10 runs for representative small models. Manual canary: landed to a staging branch and exercised against a historical regression set (Linear ENG-8821). CI logs include the diff summaries and artifact links for auditor review.

Rollout plan: merge to main, enable "eval-quality-gate" label for a subset of teams, monitor gating rate for two weeks, then flip gate to required for all eval-harness PRs.

Notes: This PR is intentionally conservative in the default thresholds; teams can opt-in via repository-level .eval-gate.yaml. Follow-up work will add automatic rollback runbooks and a lightweight UI in the Redwood Console to triage regressions.
